ClearComply

Getting Started Guide

A quick walkthrough of ClearComply for compliance managers — signing in, your dashboard, viewing subcontractor and project details, and onboarding new subcontractors and projects.

1

Sign in or create your account

ClearComply is access-controlled — every user has their own login. If you're new, click Create an account and enter your first and last name, email, and a password. Passwords must be 8–12 characters with at least one number and one special character, and no character repeated twice in a row — the live checklist turns each rule green as you meet it.

Returning users sign in with their email and password. Either way, you're placed into your organization automatically and taken straight to your dashboard.

2

Your dashboard & Action Queue

After signing in you land on the Dashboard. The five tiles across the top are your compliance pulse: percent of fully-compliant subcontractors, missing or at-risk items, documents waiting on your review, insurance expiring within 30 days, and overdue items. They update live as you act.

Below them is the Action Queue — your prioritized to-do list. Items are ranked by urgency, with overdue and rejected documents at the top, each showing its escalation status (for example, “L4 · Escalated to GC/PM — payment hold”). Use the filter chips (Needs review, Due soon, Overdue, Expiring, Rejected) to narrow the list, and act directly from each row — Send Reminder emails the subcontractor a secure link, and Review upload opens a submitted document to approve or reject.

3

The subcontractor roster

The Subcontractors tab is your full roster. Each subcontractor's four required documents — insurance, W-9, certified payroll, workforce report — show as color-coded status stamps, alongside an overall compliance score. The list is sorted least-compliant first, so whoever needs attention is always on top.

4

Opening a subcontractor's details

Click any row in the roster to slide open that subcontractor's detail panel. It shows their project and PM, the general-contractor escalation contact, every required document with its current status and next automated step, a drop zone to simulate an upload, and a full activity-log audit trail.

Click View full page for the same information in a full-screen layout. From either view you can act on each document — Send reminder, Escalate to GC, or Mark received — and every action is recorded in the activity log so you have a complete audit trail.

5

Projects & drilling into one

The Projects tab groups subcontractors by job. Each project card shows its assigned Project Manager, timeline, and the general-contractor escalation contact used when documents go overdue, alongside the project's overall compliance and at-risk counts.

Click View subcontractors on a card to drill into that project — the roster filters to just that project's subcontractors so you can focus on one job at a time. You can also switch projects any time using the project dropdown in the top bar.

6

Onboarding a subcontractor — Step 1: details

Click + New (top-right) to open the onboarding wizard, and keep the toggle on Subcontractor. Choose the project they'll work on, then enter their company name and email — these three are required. Trade, point of contact, and phone are optional. The email you enter is where their secure upload link is sent. Click Continue →.

7

Onboarding a subcontractor — Step 2: review

The review step confirms what you're about to create — the subcontractor's details and the set of documents ClearComply will start tracking for them. When it looks right, click Confirm & onboard.

8

Onboarding a subcontractor — Step 3: secure link

Done. ClearComply generates a unique, secure upload link and emails it to the subcontractor automatically. They upload their documents through it with no account required, and everything routes straight back into your review queue. You can Copy link to send it yourself, or Preview upload page to see exactly what they'll see. Their required-document set now appears on your dashboard.

9

Creating a project

To add a project, open + New and switch the toggle to Project. A unique project name is required; you can optionally add the PM, location, start and end dates, notes, and the general contractor's escalation contact (used to escalate overdue items). Click Create and the project appears in the Projects tab and the project dropdown, ready for subcontractors.

ClearComply — subcontractor compliance tracking. This guide reflects the current build.
